chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from ʿAlī ibn Aḥmad ibn Ashyam, from Abū Hārūn al-Makfūf, from the one whom he mentioned, who said:
Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said to Abū Hārūn al-Makfūf:

“What do you say, O Abū Hārūn, regarding a blind man who used to move about the town without a guide, then a man called out to him: ‘O so-and-so, the well is in front of you,’ and the blind man was unable to move away, so the blind man held on to the one who called out to him, and then said: ‘I used to move about the town and did not need a guide’?”
He عليه السلام said: “The guide is liable because of what he called out with.” Then he handed him dinars from beneath his carpet and said: “O Abū Hārūn, buy a guide with this.”

key_terms.الْبِئْرُ: the well, representing the danger ahead
key_terms.دَنَانِيرَ: gold coins given as financial assistance
key_terms.صَوَّتَ: called out or raised his voice in directing someone
key_terms.قَائِدٍ: a guide who leads and assists the blind person

ai.seo_question: Is a person legally liable for harm caused by verbally directing a blind person?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses legal liability in a case involving a blind person and one who verbally guides him near danger. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام rules that the one who called out bears responsibility because of his directing speech, and he then practically assists Abū Hārūn by giving him money to hire a guide.
